To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TBLVLTR contains an enhancer that is necessary and sufficient for T-cell-specific activation of c-myc.
the TBLVLTR enhancer is necessary and sufficient for TBLV-induced leukemogenesis and that the transcriptional coactivator ALY is a key factor in TBLV enhancerspecific transcriptional regulation.

a TBLV variant of the mouse mammary tumor retroviral enhancer is necessary and sufficient for T cell-specific c-myc activation and that a novel coactivator, ALY, is a common target for both RUNX1 and the transcription factor c-Myb in the context of this enhancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the TBLV enhancers in the induction of leukemia and lymphomas.
the identification of transcriptional cofactors that mediate oncogene activation.
the identification of a novel coactivator for the RUNX1 and the c-Myb transcription factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ALY gene encodes a protein that functions as a coactivator of RUNK1B and c-MyB in the context of a TBLV LTER.
ALY is an essential coactivator for RUNX1 and Myb on the TBLV enhancers.
the TBL enhancer contains a RUNX1 binding element, which is necessary for enhancer activity in Jurkat cells, but not sufficient to fully recapitulate TBL enhancer activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ALY is a common coactivator for RUNX1B and c-MyB on the TBLV enhancers.
ALY is a common coactivator of RUNXB1 and c- Myb on the TBLV enhancers.
ALY acts as a common coactivator of RUNNX1 and c- Myb on the TBLV enhancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ALY is a common coactivator of both RUNX1 and MYB on the TBLV enhancers.
ALY is a novel coactivator for both RUNX1 and MYB on a T-cell leukemia enhancer.
the TBLVLTR enhancer functions by recruiting ALY and RUNX1 to the enhancer region, which leads to the activation of c-myb and c-myc expression.
